recipes.title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon & Olives
recipes.dish_alt: Chicken tagine simmered with onions and herbs in a golden spiced sauce
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Ras el Hanout Spice Blend
recipes.prep_alt: A bag of ras el hanout, the warm Moroccan spice blend that seasons the tagine

sections.heading: Steps
items: Warm the olive oil in a wide heavy pot and cook the sliced onion 4-5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, ras el hanout, turmeric, saffron, and cinnamon stick, cooking 1 minute until fragrant.
Nestle the chicken into the onions and spices, turning to coat.
Pour in the stock or water, cover, and simmer low 40-45 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the preserved lemon rind and olives, and simmer uncovered 10 more minutes to thicken the sauce.
Taste and season lightly with salt (preserved lemon and olives are already salty).
Sprinkle with chopped cilantro and parsley.
Serve hot, spooning the sauce over the chicken, with warm bread or couscous.

recipes.title: Harira (Moroccan Lentil & Chickpea Soup)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of harira soup with lentils, chickpeas, and vermicelli in a spiced tomato broth
recipes.prep_alt: A pot of harira soup simmering with lentils and chickpeas, prepared at home

sections.heading: Steps
items: Cook the onion and celery in a little oil 4-5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, and saffron, cooking 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes, lentils, chickpeas, and water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a simmer, cover partway, and cook 45-60 minutes until the lentils and chickpeas are tender.
If using, stir in the vermicelli and simmer 5-8 minutes more.
Whisk the flour with a little cold water into a smooth, thin tedouira.
Drizzle the tedouira into the simmering soup while stirring, then simmer 5 more minutes until velvety.
Taste and season with salt.
Stir in the chopped cilantro and parsley.
Ladle into bowls and serve with lemon wedges and dates on the side.

recipes.title: Kefta Tagine (Spiced Meatball Tagine in Tomato Sauce)
recipes.dish_alt: Spiced meatballs simmered in a rich tomato tagine sauce, Moroccan kefta style
recipes.prep_alt: Spiced kofta patties served alongside chickpeas and couscous, the building blocks of the dish

sections.heading: Steps
items: Mix the ground meat with grated onion, half the garlic, parsley, cilantro, cumin, paprika, and cinnamon.
Roll the mixture into small, walnut-sized meatballs.
Cook the finely chopped onion in olive oil 4-5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the remaining garlic and ginger, then add the crushed tomatoes and a splash of water, simmering uncovered 10 minutes.
Lower the meatballs into the sauce, cover, and cook 15-20 minutes until cooked through.
Make small wells in the sauce between the meatballs.
Crack an egg into each well, cover, and cook 7-10 minutes until the whites set but yolks stay runny.
Sprinkle with chopped cilantro.
Serve straight from the pot with warm crusty bread.

recipes.title: Moroccan Fish Chermoula
recipes.dish_alt: Whole fish simmered in a chermoula tomato and olive sauce, Moroccan style
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Fresh Parsley for the Chermoula
recipes.prep_alt: A fresh bunch of parsley, one of the key herbs in chermoula marinade

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: White fish fillets (hake, cod, or sea bass)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Blend the cilantro, parsley, garlic, cumin, paprika, lemon juice, and olive oil into a coarse chermoula paste.
Rub the fish with about two-thirds of the chermoula and marinate in the fridge 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Warm a little oil in a wide pan and, if using, cook the bell pepper and tomato 3-4 minutes until softened.
Lay the marinated fish in the pan and cook 3-4 minutes per side until it flakes easily.
Spoon the remaining chermoula over the fish during the last minute of cooking.
Lift the fish and vegetables onto a plate.
Serve warm with lemon wedges and crusty bread or rice.

recipes.title: Moroccan Chicken with Chickpeas & Apricots
recipes.dish_alt: Chicken tagine with olives, carrots, and warm spices in a golden sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Chickpeas shown soaked (left) and dried (right), before and after their overnight soak

sections.heading: Steps
items: Cook the onion in a little oil 4-5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, coriander, turmeric, and saffron, cooking 1 minute until fragrant.
Nestle the chicken into the spiced onions, turning to coat.
Add the stock or water, bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook low 25-30 minutes.
Stir in the honey, chickpeas, and dried apricots, and simmer uncovered 15-20 minutes more until the chicken is fully cooked.
Taste and season with salt as needed.
Scatter the toasted almonds and chopped cilantro over the top.
Serve hot with couscous or warm bread.

recipes.title: Couscous with Seven Vegetables
recipes.dish_alt: A mound of fluffy couscous topped with seven simmered vegetables and raisins
recipes.prep_alt: A two-tier couscoussière pot used to steam couscous over the simmering vegetable broth

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Bone-in chicken or lamb pieces (for broth)
Pumpkin or butternut squash, cut into chunks

sections.heading: Steps
items: Cook the onion with ginger, turmeric, and saffron in a little oil 2-3 minutes, then add the tomato and cook until saucy.
Add the chicken or lamb and water to cover, bring to a boil, and skim off any foam.
Add the chickpeas, cover partway, and simmer 30-40 minutes.
Spread the dry couscous in a wide dish, drizzle with water and oil, and rub between your palms to separate every grain.
Steam the couscous uncovered over the simmering broth 15-20 minutes.
Tip the couscous back into the dish, drizzle with warm salted water, and fluff it between your palms; repeat the steaming once more for the best texture.
Add the carrot and turnip to the broth and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the zucchini, pumpkin, and cabbage, and simmer 10-15 more minutes until tender.
Mound the fluffed couscous on a platter and dot with butter, tossing to melt through.
Arrange the vegetables and chickpeas over the couscous, scatter raisins on top, and ladle a little broth over everything.
Serve the extra broth on the side for spooning over individual plates.

recipes.title: Lamb Tagine with Apricots & Almonds
recipes.dish_alt: Lamb tagine braised low and slow in a rich spiced tomato sauce
recipes.prep_alt: A pile of dried apricots, ready to plump up in the simmering lamb tagine

sections.heading: Steps
items: Season the lamb with cinnamon, cumin, saffron, and a pinch of salt.
Brown the lamb in batches in a little oil, 3-4 minutes per side, then set aside.
Cook the onion 4-5 minutes until soft, then add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Return the lamb to the pot with the water or stock, cover, and simmer low 1½-2 hours until fork-tender.
Stir in the honey and dried apricots, and simmer uncovered 30-45 minutes more until plump and the sauce thickens.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan 3-4 minutes until golden.
Taste and season with salt.
Spoon onto a platter, scatter with toasted almonds, sesame seeds, cilantro, and parsley.
Serve hot with couscous or crusty bread.

recipes.title: Moroccan Orange & Cinnamon Salad (Fenjaan) (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: Orange segments fanned on a plate, ready to be dressed with cinnamon and orange blossom water
recipes.prep_alt: A cross-section slice of a navel orange, showing its juicy segments

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Toasted almonds or chopped dates (optional garnish)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Peel the oranges down to the flesh, removing all the white pith.
Slice the oranges crosswise into thin rounds, catching any juice, and arrange on a plate.
Whisk the collected juice with the orange blossom water and honey.
Drizzle the juice mixture evenly over the orange slices.
Sprinkle the cinnamon over the top.
Scatter with mint leaves and almonds or dates, if using.
Chill at least 15 minutes before serving.
